palette_lock.rule: ALL cabin and set plates use these exact flat fills. CCTV changes only the lighting tint, NEVER the underlying seat/wall/floor colors. Chaos/barricade are the same cabin with debris added, not a new color scheme. Pass the approved p1-aisle-bg.png as <Picture 1> color reference when regenerating cabin plates.
palette_lock.cctv_tint: flat desaturated green-grey veil over the SAME navy seats and teal floor, do not recolor the objects
palette_lock.forbid: different seat navy between plates, pink/purple seats, mixed warm/cold wall tints in one cabin

lighting_contract.rule: STORYTIME HORROR at night. Create dread by lowering overall VALUE (brightness) with a few motivated light sources, NOT by repainting every surface navy. CRITICAL: do NOT make the WALL the same navy as the seats. Seats are #15233B and Khang/Vy/crew/infected all wear navy, so a navy wall makes flat-fill character-on-seat-against-wall merge into one indistinguishable mass. Keep each material a distinct VALUE/HUE so forms separate, then dim the whole frame with shadow regions.
lighting_contract.wall_value: walls and ceiling are a cool dark SLATE / dimmed bone (clearly lighter and cooler than #15233B seat navy, but NOT bright cream). They must stay visually distinct from seats and navy clothing so navy figures read against them.
lighting_contract.seat_and_character: seats and navy clothing keep #15233B; separate them from the wall by outline weight and value contrast, never by making the wall navy too
lighting_contract.teal_usage: teal only as a faint floor path / thin strip, never a broad bright floor
lighting_contract.prompt_visible: Low-key night-horror light: one small bone-white ceiling fixture visibly lit near the camera end; cool dark slate walls clearly lighter than the navy seats; 60 to 75 percent of the frame held in hard-edged flat navy shadow shapes; heavy flat four-corner vignette falling to near-black
lighting_contract.sources: 1-2 visible emitting fixtures only: dim aisle ceiling strip, a failing emergency light, or city-light dots through the oval windows; the rest of the frame (60-75%) falls into flat dark shadow shapes, no beam, no gradient spotlight, no glowing wall with no fixture
lighting_contract.vignette: heavy dark vignette on every plate; corners fall to near-black

tiers.dim_night_flight: normal night flight (p1-aisle-bg master, seat_27a): cabin is dim/creepy but structure and faces stay readable; slate walls slightly lit by ceiling fixture, teal path faint
tiers.cctv: same cabin under a faint green-grey veil plus darker corners, like a monitor feed; objects keep their colors
tiers.failure: chaos/barricade: main lights dead or flickering, only floor/emergency strips or one harsh broken fixture; deep contrast, 70%+ of frame in shadow, much darker than dim_night_flight

lighting_contract.restaurant_exception: restaurant flashback keeps a flat warm amber tint on furniture only, no light beam or glow, still darker at the edges
lighting_contract.forbid: navy walls matching the seats, uniform bright bone walls, bright teal full floor, glowing surface with no fixture, gradient beams, pink/purple rim light, any frame that reads as daytime

state_chain.rule: Variants of one set must inherit BOTH color (palette_lock) AND object form/state from the master plate and the previous state. Passing only a color reference is NOT enough: it causes design drift (same color, wrong shape) and prop discontinuity (objects vanish or mutate between states).
state_chain.order: Atomic character/prop refs (qa_passed) -> Master plate p1-aisle-bg.png (qa_passed) -> variants in time order: CCTV -> chaos -> barricade. Each variant references the previous qa_passed state and changes ONLY the declared state_delta.

generation_prompt_contract: Begin: 'Vertical 9:16 flat 2D storytime horror BACKGROUND PLATE, EMPTY SCENE, one continuous space, one viewpoint, one-point depth, no panels, no borders, no text.'
Then paste the scene's geometry sentence verbatim from this file.

Then paste the scene's objects and light sentences verbatim, naming every object together with the surface that supports it. For night-cabin plates the light sentence must come from lighting_contract.tiers (dim_night_flight by default, failure for chaos): low-key, one or two motivated fixtures, slate walls lighter than navy seats, 60-75 percent flat shadow and a heavy flat vignette - never even fill.
Then add: 'Build depth with three flat layers (foreground / midground / background), distinct value tiers and visible occlusions; solid flat fills with at most two tone values per surface.'
End: 'Extra thick uneven black ink outlines, palette near-black navy / bone white / one muted teal, red only for blood and recording dot, no gradient, no shading, no texture, not realistic, not 3D.'
Do not delete an object with a negation. Describe the intended object count and placement positively; keep forbidden facts in this map for QA only.

Copy seat count, axis, window side and light values from master_plate / lighting_contract. Never hardcode a convention from memory: exactly two rows of 1+1 (four seats total) is canonical by user decision 26/11, pending QA master r6. A 2+2 reading would create eight seats and is FAIL under the new design.
For every flat cabin plate, <Picture 1> is master_plate.path with latest verdict PASS. The 3D route map supplies topology as TEXT only and is never injected as an image ref into a flat plate.
When red_allowed=false, omit the word red entirely - including the old 'red only for blood and recording dot' clause, which primed two red dots in G02.

Compose prompts with art/tests/h3_prompt_rules.py + art/tests/story_to_asset_prompts.py and run art/tests/check_asset_prompt.py before gen_image.py. One job = one asset. Sole user-approved waiver (26/11): one crowd sheet holding exactly four distinct generic seated figures in a single equal-width row may replace four separate character files; it must never carry Khang or Vy identity and must be QA'd as four figures, one row, no cropped edge.
Never write 'storybook page', 'comic panel', 'sequence', or 'multiple views' — they produce a 6-panel page (measured on v3-r1-restaurant.png).

For a cabin variant, first pass every required_refs[plate] id from state_chain (base_plate + form_refs + cast_refs) that has qa_passed=true and label each <Picture N> by its role; then paste the palette_lock hex values verbatim; then describe only the state_delta. A variant with no refs is a HARD FAIL, not a warning.
revision_note: User decision 26/11/2026: backgrounds are DEEPER (layered flat cut-paper depth, one-point perspective, visible supports/occlusions, distinct value tiers) while characters stay strictly flat. v4.1 syncs the light contract into global-context/rebuilt prompts: a horror film is low-key (one or two motivated fixtures, slate walls distinct from navy seats, 60-75 percent flat shadow, heavy flat vignette) - never evenly lit. v3 spec has 60 shots (G01-G24 / P2G01-P2G24 / P3G01-P3G12) and contains no restaurant scene.
design_change_20261126: User approved exactly two rows / four seats (1+1 per row), a one-row four-figure generic crowd sheet composited into the three seats other than 27A, and Khang retained in 27A. The 2-row/4-seat label means 1+1, NOT 2+2; any prompt saying 2+2 or eight seats is FAIL.

depth_contract.rule: Background depth comes from flat geometry only: distinct foreground / midground / background planes, one-point perspective, visible occlusion, object-to-support contact and 2-3 flat value tiers. No gradient, no shading, no texture, no beam, no photorealism.
depth_contract.character_rule: Characters remain strict flat storybook shapes: solid fills, two dot eyes, one mouth line, four-finger flat hands with a thumb, adult 1:6 full-body proportions with flat segmented shoulders, elbows, hips and knees, no modelling or shading.
depth_contract.qa_eye: Hy4 is the read-only description-only eye for every generated asset. The agent writes the PASS/FAIL verdict only after Hy4 has described the file.

invariants: exactly two rows (27 and 28) with four seats total, one seat on each side of the aisle in every row
seat 27A is the left window seat and stays empty in the plate; Khang and three generic passengers are added later at the compositing stage
1+1 navy seats with slate headrests and armrests; same shape in every plate
one centered aisle running front-near to tail-far, never flipped
oval windows on BOTH sides, one per row, aligned with the window seats; never square
closed overhead bins above the seats; one motivated ceiling fixture; muted-teal floor path
60 to 75 percent shadow built from hard-edged flat navy shapes and a heavy four-corner vignette
master_plate.layout_prompt: Exactly two seat rows in one continuous cabin: one near row and one far row. Draw exactly four seat silhouettes in total, one single seat on the left and one single seat on the right in the near row, one single seat on the left and one single seat on the right in the far row; each single seat touches the oval wall window on its outer side and the aisle on its inner side. Leave a large empty dark floor area between the near row and the camera. One straight muted-teal aisle runner runs from the near bottom edge to the far tail door between the four seats. Seat 27A is the single left-window seat of the near row. Exactly four oval windows total: one in the left wall and one in the right wall beside each of the two rows, all oval and aligned with their seats. Closed overhead bins rest directly above the four seats. One small bone-white ceiling fixture is visibly lit near the camera end. The single closed tail-lavatory door stands at the far vanishing point with one small bright bone-white square window and one black round knob directly below it.
master_plate.compositing_note: QA metadata only, never prompt text: row numbers are 27 (near) and 28 (far); Khang and three generic passengers are composited later, not drawn by H3.
master_plate.deviation_note: 26/11/2026 user redesign: exactly two rows and four seats total, one seat per side (1+1). The former 3+3, five-row and 2+2-per-row conventions are retired; the old r4 master is missing on disk and r5/r5d/r5e are archived. Master r6 FAILED QA (3 rows x 4 seats, 8 windows, fixture at far end) and is not canonical. Master r7 PASSED QA and IS canonical: Hy4 3 rounds saw exactly 4 seat backs in 2 rows of 1+1, 4 oval windows, fixture near the camera and one teal aisle; machine 53 colors / 65 percent shadow / 0 red. Residual soft tone around the fixture and in the wall vignette is tolerated at plate level but must not spread into seats/floor/walls in rendered frames; the r7 seats are single navy blocks, so seat-variant prompts must state the slate headrest and armrest forms explicitly.
